title: Spitballs with Dizzy during the Cab Drivers' number
summary: While Cab changed costumes, Jones, Dizzy and Chu Berry shot paper wads at Cozy Cole during the Cab Drivers' spot, a game repeated across theaters until Cab saw it.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Well, Jonah, were you there when Diz hit him with the chair, or whatever?

When he -- when he was supposed to be cutting him with a knife. Yeah, well, this was a silly thing, too. Musicians are always kidding around. We was at the State Theater up there, in Hartford, and all the time me and Dizzy have been rolling up paper wads all during the show, you know, spitballs they call them. And so when Cab would go off the stand to change, three or four times, you know, during one show. He'd come on with a tux, and you'd see him again, he's got on a white tux. Next time he's got on all blue, blue shoes. And the next time, tan shoes. So he changed. So now, when the Cab Drivers went out there, that was Tyree, Danny Parker, Benny Payne, Cozy and Milt Hinton. No, that's the little band out of the big band. The Palmer Brothers you're [Addressing Stanley Dance] thinking about. These are the Cab Drivers.
The Cab Drivers. How cute. The Cab Drivers.

Yeah, the Cab Jivers. And what we'd do, now when they come out, then he'd go off to change clothes. Now, me and Diz got all these paper wads or spitballs, and we'd be shooting -- and Ch Berry was in on this -- so we'd be shooting and grabbing our heads, Cozy would be playing and grabbing his head, and Cab come back out there. It was a big

stage. We used to play in some big houses. We used to play some better houses than Duke. See, we'd play in Chicago, we'd play the Chicago Theater and Duke would be around at the Oriental, you know. Because they'd all be at the same office, you know. We were all out of the same office. He would get some of the lesser ones, and I couldn't figure that out for nothing. As much as them guys play over there and we don't have that kind of music, but I guess it takes you a long time to figure some things that are right before you. But Cab was visual. Duke was sound.
